findings.title: Unauthenticated decompression bomb in load_payload exhausts server memory
findings.description:
Entry: src/itsdangerous/serializer.py:392 (Serializer._loads_unsafe_impl passes the unverified payload to load_payload) and src/itsdangerous/url_safe.py:23 (URLSafeSerializerMixin.load_payload), also reached by the documented BadSignature recovery pattern at docs/serializer.rst:58.
Attacker: an unauthenticated caller who controls a token string submitted to an application that reads it with URLSafeSerializer.loads_unsafe or URLSafeTimedSerializer.loads_unsafe, or that follows the documented "catch BadSignature, then s.load_payload(e.payload)" pattern; the boundary crossed is signature verification, which those public APIs deliberately skip.
Path: attacker token -> Serializer.loads_unsafe (serializer.py:349) -> _loads_unsafe_impl (serializer.py:367-395); when the HMAC check fails, e.payload, the raw value before the separator that was never verified, is passed to URLSafeSerializerMixin.load_payload (url_safe.py:23) -> base64_decode (url_safe.py:37) -> zlib.decompress (url_safe.py:46) -> JSON parse.
Nothing on the path caps the decompressed size: load_payload only strips the leading '.' compression marker, base64-decodes, and calls zlib.decompress, which allocates the entire output in one bytes object; zlib's maximum expansion ratio is about 1032:1, so a ~1 MB token of compressed bytes inflates to ~1 GB of memory, and a request body of a few MB exhausts the worker. The ordinary loads path is safe because Signer.unsign verifies the HMAC first (serializer.py:339, timed.py:204), but the unsafe/recovery paths call load_payload on data whose signature was never checked, and the JSON serializer that users are told is safe to use with loads_unsafe gives no protection because the amplification happens inside the library's own URLSafe mixin before the JSON serializer is invoked.
Impact: a small, cheap, repeatable unauthenticated request causes a multi-hundred-fold memory and CPU amplification, terminating or destabilizing the server process; the docstring's warning only covers the payload serializer (pickle), not this internal decompression step.
Fix: decompress with a hard output cap, e.g. d = zlib.decompressobj(); out = d.decompress(data, MAX_PAYLOAD); reject when d.unconsumed_tail or len(out) == MAX_PAYLOAD, make the cap configurable, and do not call load_payload on an unverified payload from loads_unsafe without applying that cap.
